about: US-16 section 6, analogy sweep: what comparable projects usually need or get wrong. Data, tenant-agnostic. `source` is null unless a real URL is supplied: the audit then records 'no source', never an invented citation. Items on professional topics are risks marked needs_professional and are not gate cards unless blocking is true (the system gives no legal, medical, financial or safety advice).

items.item: Who can change or read what: a contact for reporting a security problem, and access limited to the people who need it
Pages that people using a screen reader, a keyboard only or large text can use, with a statement saying so
How long personal details are kept and how a person asks for them to be removed
What happens when it breaks, who is told, and a backup that has been restored at least once
A monthly cost limit and what the system does when it is close to the limit
Who looks after it if the owner is away for a long time
Mail sent in the project's name that receiving servers can verify
The web address stays registered: who renews it and when
A privacy notice and terms of use for the visitors the idea touches
Whether the chosen name is already used by someone else
Tax obligations if the project takes money or runs as a business
The licences of the software the project is built from allow how it will be used
